newsitem.title: USA: Florida Panthers sued by some shareholders.
newsitem.headline: Florida Panthers sued by some shareholders.

text.p: A class-action lawsuit was filed against Florida Panthers Holdings Inc accusing it of offering dismal forecasts that hurt selling shareholders, but ultimately benefitted some officers when the stock price tripled in a one-month period, lawyers for the plaintiffs said Tuesday night.

The lawsuit was filed Tuesday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida on behalf of individuals who sold their stock in Florida Panthers, which owns the football team by the same name, between November 13, 1996 and December 22, 1996.
The company could not be reached immediately for comment.
Stan Smith, a spokesman for Chairman H. Wayne Huizenga, told Reuters: "We would not make comment on pending litigation."
The plaintiffs are being represented by the New York law firm of Wolf Haldenstein Adler Freeman & Herz LLP.

In a news release issued Tuesday night, the lawyers contend the company and some of its officers "gave a false impression of the company's potential for the next two to three years and about the intended direction that the company was going take."

In particular, the plaintiffs fault statements by the company that it had "significant cash flow problems and that historically sports franchises struggled financially for their first few years", as well as allegedly "failing to indicate that the company would embark on a program of purchases to transform it into a "leisure-time-based sports and entertainment company."
The plaintiffs said the defendants bought 285,000 shares of Florida Panthers stock at "prices close to the $10 mark."
